I fixed the AllocateQuota function in repair.go by correcting the tie-breaking logic in the sorting algorithm. 

The issue was in the `sort.SliceStable` function call where, when two requests had equal fractional remainders, it was using `shares[i].index < shares[j].index` to break ties. This caused the wrong allocation order because it was sorting by array index rather than by the actual request ID.

The fix changes the tie-breaking logic to use `requests[shares[i].index].ID < requests[shares[j].index].ID` which properly sorts by the lexicographic order of the request IDs. This ensures that when there's a tie in fractional remainders, the request with the smaller ID gets priority, which matches the expected behavior in the test case.
